research_questions.md.title: Overview & multi-scale hypothesis
research_questions.md.input: Lymphoma tissue images, expert staining grades and supplied subtype labels.
research_questions.md.framing: Whole-slide lymphoma scans are too large to train on directly. If we extract each specimen at three biological scales (cores, patches, cells) and compress them into feature vectors, which scale best predicts (1) expert staining grades and (2) molecular subtypes—and can we trace predictions back onto the tissue?

README.md.title: Replay the grading workflow
README.md.input: The published adaptations, their generated inputs and the grading example.
README.md.framing: Can a reviewer rerun the entire three-scale grading workflow from one command and inspect every intermediate CSV and SVG chart?

select_core_rectangles.py.title: Draw manual core boxes
select_core_rectangles.py.input: Two hand-drawn preview boxes and the zoom factors linking the preview to the full scan.
select_core_rectangles.py.framing: Drawing a rectangle around each tissue core kept a person in control of every selection, at the cost of 6 seconds per core and uneven box dimensions.
select_core_rectangles.py.method: Scale each hand-drawn preview rectangle (left, top, width, height) by the slide zoom multiplier and display magnification.

interpolate_core_grid.py.title: Project a tilted microarray grid
interpolate_core_grid.py.input: Two corner reference clicks on a tilted microarray and the observed centres of four cores.
interpolate_core_grid.py.framing: Could two corner clicks define the tilt and spacing of an entire microarray grid in 0.5 seconds per core—and what breaks when a core drifts off the grid line?
interpolate_core_grid.py.method: Estimate slide tilt angle and row spacing from two reference clicks, project square bounds across rows and columns, and measure centre drift.

prepare_image_regions.py.title: Mark core centres with 1 click
prepare_image_regions.py.input: A generated tissue-core image and the point you mark.
prepare_image_regions.py.framing: Manual boxes took 6 seconds with uneven sizes, while a projected grid clipped off-grid cores. Can one click mark each centre and cut a uniform 5,000 × 5,000 px square?
prepare_image_regions.py.method: Save top, bottom, left and right pixel bounds around each clicked centre (clamping inward at scan edges), and separately tile an extracted core into regular grid patches.

crop_benchmark.csv.title: Benchmark 4 core-finding methods
crop_benchmark.csv.input: Four extraction methods compared in the submitted thesis (Table 2.5, p. 70).
crop_benchmark.csv.framing: How do Hough circles, tilted grid projection, manual boxes and 1-click cropping compare on speed, precision, recall and crop uniformity?
crop_benchmark.csv.method: Compare measured time per sample, precision (no wrong selections), recall (no missed cores) and manual intervention across all four core-extraction methods.

record_crop_marks.py.title: Save scan crop coordinates
record_crop_marks.py.input: Two named marks on one generated scan, each with a centre and rectangle.
record_crop_marks.py.framing: How do we record clicked centres and rectangle bounds in a lightweight CSV manifest before touching the multi-gigabyte pixel files?

extract_labelled_crops.py.title: Cut out cores with a manifest
extract_labelled_crops.py.input: An example image and two labelled sets of pixel bounds.
extract_labelled_crops.py.framing: Once core bounds are recorded, how do we extract each core image while keeping a permanent link to its parent scan coordinates?

map_crop_to_scan.py.title: Map crop boxes back to full scan
map_crop_to_scan.py.input: An example box on a reduced image, together with its offset and scale.
map_crop_to_scan.py.framing: If a model highlights a 20 × 20 px box inside a 4× downsampled crop, where does that box sit on the full-resolution whole-slide scan?

filter_tissue_patches.py.title: Filter empty background tiles
filter_tissue_patches.py.input: I used a generated mask to illustrate the filter. Each of its eight tiles is kept if at least half of it contains tissue.
filter_tissue_patches.py.framing: A full bounding grid over a circular core cuts across empty glass as well as tissue. Which grid squares contain enough tissue (≥ 50%) to keep?

summarise_patch_counts.py.title: Flag cores with zero usable patches
summarise_patch_counts.py.input: A list of expected cores and the manifest of saved patches.
summarise_patch_counts.py.framing: If a damaged or faintly stained core yields zero usable patches after background filtering, how do we catch it before training starts?

extract_patch_images.py.title: Save patch tiles with bounds
extract_patch_images.py.input: Generated image regions and their measured tissue coverage.
extract_patch_images.py.framing: How do we export accepted patch tiles so every image file carries its source core ID, pixel bounds and tissue fraction?

extract_cell_crops.py.title: Extract size-filtered cell crops
extract_cell_crops.py.input: A generated image and labelled regions, with the allowed size range for retaining a cell.
extract_cell_crops.py.framing: Instance segmentation masks include tiny stain specks and giant vacuoles alongside real cells. How do we filter by diameter and cut uniform cell crops?

index_segmented_cells.py.title: Index cells to global scan coords
index_segmented_cells.py.role: Add core origin to cell offsets
index_segmented_cells.py.input: Two segmented cells and the coordinates of their containing core.
index_segmented_cells.py.framing: How do we convert each segmented cell's local crop offset into exact global (x, y) coordinates on the whole-slide scan?

package_cell_arrays.py.title: Pack aligned cell arrays
package_cell_arrays.py.input: Two cell IDs, their x/y positions and one feature per cell.
package_cell_arrays.py.framing: With 9.13 million segmented cells, how do we store cell IDs, coordinates and feature vectors in one compressed archive without row misalignment?

summarise_cells_by_core.py.title: Audit cell counts across cores
summarise_cells_by_core.py.input: A generated cell index spread across three cores.
summarise_cells_by_core.py.framing: Does a total cell count hide the fact that one dense core supplies most of the cells while another core has zero?

compare_image_encodings.py.title: Compare PNG vs WebP compression
compare_image_encodings.py.input: The same generated patch saved using PNG and WebP.
compare_image_encodings.py.framing: How much storage did WebP save in the thesis, and how does a small generated example measure changes in decoded pixels?

audit_dataset_structure.py.title: Audit dataset shapes before training
audit_dataset_structure.py.input: An expected file inventory and a dataset with deliberate omissions and shape mismatches.
audit_dataset_structure.py.framing: How do we catch missing feature files, unexpected spillover files or truncated array dimensions before a multi-hour GPU job starts?

measure_storage_reads.py.title: Time bundled vs separate file reads
measure_storage_reads.py.input: Identical generated bytes stored in separate files and in one bundle.
measure_storage_reads.py.framing: Does seeking inside one contiguous binary file reduce filesystem overhead compared with opening dozens of small patch files?

fit_linear_autoencoder.py.title: Compress patches via reconstruction
fit_linear_autoencoder.py.input: Three generated patches and a two-feature target width.
fit_linear_autoencoder.py.framing: An autoencoder squeezes each patch into a short numerical code and tries to rebuild the image. Which input details survive that narrow bottleneck?

score_reconstructions.py.title: Rank worst reconstructions first
score_reconstructions.py.input: Two pairs of original and reconstructed example arrays.
score_reconstructions.py.framing: An average reconstruction error hides individual failures. How do we rank held-out patches worst-first so high-residual anomalies are inspected immediately?

compare_bottleneck_sizes.py.title: Compare code width vs reconstruction error
compare_bottleneck_sizes.py.role: Trade off 16 B vs 32 B latent codes
compare_bottleneck_sizes.py.input: The same example input and two candidate widths for its compressed representation.
compare_bottleneck_sizes.py.framing: How much reconstruction fidelity do we gain on held-out patches when we double the latent bottleneck width?

score_variational_reconstruction.py.title: Split VAE pixel loss from KL penalty
score_variational_reconstruction.py.input: A generated reconstruction, its target and the statistics of its compressed code.
score_variational_reconstruction.py.framing: When a variational autoencoder's total loss changes, how do we tell whether image reconstruction improved or the latent KL penalty shifted?

learn_image_features.py.title: Penalise redundant feature columns
learn_image_features.py.input: Paired feature vectors for four generated samples.
learn_image_features.py.framing: Two augmented views can agree perfectly even if the encoder copies the same number into every column. How does Barlow Twins penalise redundant columns?

prepare_paired_views.py.title: Generate paired augmented views
prepare_paired_views.py.role: Create linked views per patch ID
prepare_paired_views.py.input: One identified patch and two image transformations.
prepare_paired_views.py.framing: How do we apply stochastic flips and brightness shifts to create two distinct views of each patch while keeping their shared patch ID intact?

audit_feature_variation.py.title: Detect collapsed or duplicate features
audit_feature_variation.py.input: An example matrix with one column per feature across multiple patches.
audit_feature_variation.py.framing: Before training downstream classifiers, how do we verify that no feature column collapsed to a constant or duplicated another column?

fit_shared_view_encoder.py.title: Train a shared encoder on paired views
fit_shared_view_encoder.py.input: Two generated versions of the same examples and a shared encoder trained for 40 updates.
fit_shared_view_encoder.py.framing: Can one shared weight matrix learn features that stay invariant across paired views while driving off-diagonal redundancy toward zero?

batch_frozen_features.py.title: Extract frozen features in batches
batch_frozen_features.py.role: Preserve patch ID order across batches
batch_frozen_features.py.input: Three identified example patches and a fixed feature extractor.
batch_frozen_features.py.framing: How do we run hundreds of thousands of patches through a frozen pretrained backbone in batches while guaranteeing exact input ID order?

compare_encoder_dimensions.py.title: Compare 16-D vs 64-D vector footprints
compare_encoder_dimensions.py.input: Two candidate vector widths and the same set of 30 examples.
compare_encoder_dimensions.py.framing: How much memory and cache footprint do we save when choosing a narrower feature vector width across a cohort?

standardise_encoder_inputs.py.title: Standardise RGB inputs for backbones
standardise_encoder_inputs.py.input: An RGB image and an encoder’s target dimensions and colour-channel scaling.
standardise_encoder_inputs.py.framing: Pretrained backbones expect fixed input dimensions and channel statistics. How do we standardise arbitrary histology crops into normalised float32 tensors?

benchmark_frozen_features.py.title: Benchmark encoders on shared splits
benchmark_frozen_features.py.input: Two generated feature sets, training labels and a shared test split.
benchmark_frozen_features.py.framing: When comparing two candidate feature extractors, how do we lock the training centroids and held-out test split so the comparison is fair?

measure_feature_separation.py.title: Score cluster separation (Silhouette)
measure_feature_separation.py.input: Four example vectors from one representation, divided into two groups.
measure_feature_separation.py.framing: How tightly do examples from the same biological group cluster together relative to the nearest rival group in feature space?

project_feature_space.py.title: Project features onto 2D PCA axes
project_feature_space.py.input: Three labelled example vectors and a fitted two-axis projection.
project_feature_space.py.framing: When we project high-dimensional feature vectors onto two 2D axes for visual inspection, how much of the original variance is preserved on each axis?

check_bag_classifier_on_known_signal.py.title: Detect 1 positive patch in a 12-patch bag
check_bag_classifier_on_known_signal.py.input: Sixty-four generated sets of 12 patches with a known planted signal.
check_bag_classifier_on_known_signal.py.framing: If only 1 of 12 patches in a positive bag carries the diagnostic signal, does mean pooling dilute it—and can max pooling isolate it?

export_feature_vectors.py.title: Export vectors with pixel bounds
export_feature_vectors.py.input: Two identified patches, their coordinates and two values per vector.
export_feature_vectors.py.framing: How do we export extracted feature vectors so their source scan coordinates travel in the exact same table row?

align_features_to_regions.py.title: Join vectors to regions by ID
align_features_to_regions.py.input: Two sets of records with the same region IDs, in potentially different orders.
align_features_to_regions.py.framing: If a cluster job writes feature vectors in a different row order from the region manifest, how do we realign them safely by ID?

check_feature_cache.py.title: Verify cached features before reuse
check_feature_cache.py.role: Check ID order, encoder name & shape
check_feature_cache.py.input: A cached array, expected encoder name, region order and vector length.
check_feature_cache.py.framing: Before reusing a cached feature matrix for a new model run, how do we verify that its encoder version, row order and dimensions match the spec?

prepare_reference_grades.py.title: Average expert grades & log rater count
prepare_reference_grades.py.input: Three generated assessor ratings for two samples.
prepare_reference_grades.py.framing: A rating spread of 0.0 could mean two experts agreed perfectly or only one expert scored the core. Why must rater count (n) always sit beside the mean grade?

assign_validation_folds.py.title: Assign group-aware validation folds
assign_validation_folds.py.role: Keep paired samples in the same fold
assign_validation_folds.py.input: Four example samples with known grouping IDs and two destination folds.
assign_validation_folds.py.framing: How do we assign cross-validation folds so cores from the same patient or group never leak across the train/test boundary?

train_scale_graders.py.title: Train patch and cell graders
train_scale_graders.py.role: Compare scales on shared held-out split
train_scale_graders.py.input: Generated features at two image scales with shared training and test IDs.
train_scale_graders.py.framing: When trained on the exact same specimen split, which biological scale predicts held-out staining grades with the lowest error?

save_held_out_grades.py.title: Save out-of-fold grade predictions
save_held_out_grades.py.input: Predictions, reference grades and fold assignments for the example cases.
save_held_out_grades.py.framing: How do we record cross-validation predictions so every single specimen is evaluated exclusively by a model that never saw it during training?

summarise_errors_by_grade.py.title: Break down signed bias by grade
summarise_errors_by_grade.py.input: Five example predictions and their reference grades.
summarise_errors_by_grade.py.framing: Overall MAE hides directional bias at the scale ends. Does the grader pull Grade 0 upward (+0.45) and Grade 3 downward (−0.55)?

compare_experiments.py.title: Compare paired runs across folds
compare_experiments.py.role: Report paired % Δ in error, time & RAM
compare_experiments.py.input: Example runs with fold and seed IDs, error, time and memory measurements.
compare_experiments.py.framing: When a compact model change alters accuracy, runtime and memory simultaneously, how do we pair runs by fold and seed to measure the exact trade-off?

plan_matched_runs.py.title: Expand a single-change ablation grid
plan_matched_runs.py.input: A baseline, two single-change configurations and shared folds and seeds.
plan_matched_runs.py.framing: How do we generate an ablation schedule where each variant changes only one parameter from the baseline across identical folds and seeds?

verify_run_configuration.py.title: Audit startup logs against planned specs
verify_run_configuration.py.input: One planned configuration and the settings that an example run recorded at startup.
verify_run_configuration.py.framing: What if a script silently falls back to a default hyperparameter? How do we verify recorded startup logs against the planned run specification?

summarise_matched_training_traces.py.title: Compare fixed final-epoch windows
summarise_matched_training_traces.py.input: Four matched runs with per-epoch validation scores and elapsed time.
summarise_matched_training_traces.py.framing: Cherry-picking the single best validation epoch can flatter a noisy run. How do two configurations compare over a fixed final-epoch window?

weight_grading_examples.py.title: Boost rare grades & high-loss cases
weight_grading_examples.py.input: Four reference grades, their losses and previous weights.
weight_grading_examples.py.framing: Can a dynamic training sampler revisit both rare staining grades and high-loss examples without oscillating wildly between epochs?

probe_grading_model_with_noise.py.title: Probe null class with Gaussian noise
probe_grading_model_with_noise.py.role: Check noise rejection in a three-class demo
probe_grading_model_with_noise.py.input: Twelve generated signal sets and twelve noise sets for the outside-input class.
probe_grading_model_with_noise.py.framing: Can a generated three-class scorer flag noise as outside its expected inputs? The thesis used an eighth class for this purpose.

compare_assessor_errors.py.title: Compare model MAE with human rater gap
compare_assessor_errors.py.input: Two samples with matched assessor grades and model predictions.
compare_assessor_errors.py.framing: How does the patch model's error against the consensus grade (0.238 MAE) compare with the disagreement between two human experts scoring the same cores (0.382)?

score_ordinal_agreement.py.title: Score quadratic-weighted kappa (κ)
score_ordinal_agreement.py.input: Four paired grades where differences of several levels count more than one.
score_ordinal_agreement.py.framing: Mistaking Grade 0 for Grade 3 is far worse than mistaking Grade 1 for Grade 2. How does quadratic-weighted κ score ordinal agreement beyond chance?

join_subtype_labels.py.title: Match specimens to ABC / GCB labels
join_subtype_labels.py.input: Three example image IDs and a separate list of supplied subtype labels.
join_subtype_labels.py.framing: When joining image IDs to clinical subtype tables, how do we keep valid {'ABC', 'GCB'} calls while separating 'unclassified' strings from missing records?

audit_cohort_filters.py.title: Log per-rule cohort exclusions
audit_cohort_filters.py.input: Two generated specimens and a set of eligibility rules.
audit_cohort_filters.py.framing: Instead of silently dropping ineligible specimens, how do we log every pass/fail criterion per specimen so the cohort funnel (1,109 → 962) is fully auditable?

pool_patch_evidence.py.title: Compare mean, max & attention pooling
pool_patch_evidence.py.role: Combine patch vectors into 1 bag vector
pool_patch_evidence.py.input: Three generated patch features and three rules for combining them.
pool_patch_evidence.py.framing: One core contains hundreds of patches but only one subtype label. How do mean, maximum and softmax-attention pooling weight the patches inside a bag?

batch_variable_patch_sets.py.title: Sort patch sets to reduce padding
batch_variable_patch_sets.py.role: Group similar bag sizes + mask pad slots
batch_variable_patch_sets.py.input: Four specimens that contain different numbers of patches.
batch_variable_patch_sets.py.framing: Cores yield anywhere from 87 to 300+ patches. How much dummy padding do we eliminate by sorting bags by length before batching—and masking padded slots?

predict_subtypes_from_bags.py.title: Classify held-out bags by subtype
predict_subtypes_from_bags.py.role: Score bag distance to ABC vs GCB centroids
predict_subtypes_from_bags.py.input: Two labelled training sets of patches and one generated test set.
predict_subtypes_from_bags.py.framing: Once variable patch bags are pooled into specimen vectors, how do we fit a bag-level subtype classifier on training cases and score held-out bags?

compare_spatial_attention.py.title: Ablate 2D rotary patch positions (RoPE)
compare_spatial_attention.py.role: Test positions off vs on (negative result)
compare_spatial_attention.py.input: One set of example patch features with two positional arrangements.
compare_spatial_attention.py.framing: Does rotating transformer attention keys by 2D (x, y) patch coordinates change the pooled score—and did it improve subtype accuracy in the thesis?

compare_flat_and_hierarchical_pooling.py.title: Compare flat cell vs patch-then-core pooling
compare_flat_and_hierarchical_pooling.py.input: Four generated cell values, their patch memberships and a mask for empty slots.
compare_flat_and_hierarchical_pooling.py.framing: Why does averaging all cells directly let one cell-dense patch dominate the core score compared with pooling cells within each patch first?

summarise_validation.py.title: Report grading & subtype scores by fold
summarise_validation.py.input: Example held-out predictions and references for both grading and subtyping.
summarise_validation.py.framing: A single pooled average can hide a weak validation fold. How do both clinical tasks perform when broken down fold by fold?

evaluate_subtype_roc.py.title: Trace tie-aware ROC curves & AUC
evaluate_subtype_roc.py.input: Four example subtype scores and their known binary labels.
evaluate_subtype_roc.py.framing: How do true-positive and false-positive rates trade off across classification thresholds—and how must tied prediction scores (0.60) be handled?

compare_fold_class_recall.py.title: Report per-fold ABC & GCB recall (k/n)
compare_fold_class_recall.py.role: Pair class recall with explicit counts
compare_fold_class_recall.py.input: Two example folds with subtype predictions and reference labels.
compare_fold_class_recall.py.framing: Did a model achieve 50% accuracy by getting every ABC case right and every GCB case wrong? Why must class recall always show explicit k/n counts?

estimate_representation_cost.py.title: Compare raw RGB vs vector cache bytes
estimate_representation_cost.py.input: Five hundred example regions, with their raw image dimensions and feature vector size.
estimate_representation_cost.py.framing: How much storage and memory bandwidth do we save across 500 regions by caching 256-D float32 feature vectors instead of 224 × 224 RGB patches?

rank_accuracy_compute_tradeoffs.py.title: Filter models on the Pareto frontier
rank_accuracy_compute_tradeoffs.py.input: Three candidates described by accuracy, time and memory.
rank_accuracy_compute_tradeoffs.py.framing: When choosing among encoders and architectures, which candidates sit on the Pareto frontier of accuracy (↑), runtime (↓) and peak RAM (↓)?

audit_compute_measurements.py.title: Audit timing & peak RAM logs
audit_compute_measurements.py.role: Separate missing RAM logs from missing runs
audit_compute_measurements.py.input: Two example runs with their expected time and memory fields.
audit_compute_measurements.py.framing: Before plotting compute trade-offs, how do we verify that every scheduled run recorded both wall-clock runtime and peak memory?

map_patch_scores.py.title: Project patch scores onto a 2D grid
map_patch_scores.py.input: Two example patch scores and their bounds on a four-by-three grid.
map_patch_scores.py.framing: When overlapping patches are projected back onto a core's coordinate grid, how do we average overlaps while keeping unscored pixels explicitly marked as NaN?

render_score_overlay.py.title: Render heatmaps with hatched NaN areas
render_score_overlay.py.role: Shared colour scale + hatched unscored regions
render_score_overlay.py.input: A generated 64 × 48 pixel image with two overlapping scored patches.
render_score_overlay.py.framing: Where do higher and lower model scores fall on the image, and which areas were never scored?
render_score_overlay.py.method: Average scores where patch bounds overlap, render scored pixels on a shared RGBA colour scale, and hatch pixels that received no score (NaN).

summarise_overlay_coverage.py.title: Summarise scored ROI coverage
summarise_overlay_coverage.py.input: Three reference points in a region and their available scores.
summarise_overlay_coverage.py.framing: Before interpreting a heatmap over a region of interest (ROI), what fraction of the ROI actually received a model score?

explain_prediction.py.title: Fit class-specific dimming masks
explain_prediction.py.role: Spectral Dream Dimming (Class A vs B)
explain_prediction.py.input: Four generated image regions and an illustrative two-class model.
explain_prediction.py.framing: Which tissue regions must stay bright to support Class A, and which regions flip the network toward Class B when dimmed?

model_explanations.md.title: Scope XAI masks vs biological proof
model_explanations.md.input: Example masks, original scores and scores after dimming selected regions.
model_explanations.md.framing: What does a perturbation or dimming mask prove about the trained network—and what independent evidence is required before making a biological claim?

test_mask_score_changes.py.title: Test targeted vs uniform dimming control
test_mask_score_changes.py.role: 3.5× larger score drop at equal 0.80 brightness
test_mask_score_changes.py.input: An example explanation mask and an evenly dimmed mask with the same average brightness.
test_mask_score_changes.py.framing: Does dimming the highlighted region drop the model's score substantially more than dimming the entire image uniformly to the exact same 0.80 mean brightness?

compare_patch_perturbations.py.title: Compare leave-one-out vs singleton repeat
compare_patch_perturbations.py.role: Measure Δ score when removing vs repeating
compare_patch_perturbations.py.input: Three generated patches and a fixed rule for scoring the set.
compare_patch_perturbations.py.framing: How much does each patch move the bag prediction when we remove it (leave-one-out) versus when we fill the bag with copies of that single patch?

build_cluster_run_manifest.py.title: Generate SHA-256 cluster run IDs
build_cluster_run_manifest.py.input: Two configurations, two folds and two seeds to expand into a run plan.
build_cluster_run_manifest.py.framing: How do we give every cluster job a deterministic 16-character SHA-256 ID from its canonical parameters so runs never overwrite or duplicate each other?

resume_chunked_experiment.py.title: Resume interrupted jobs from checkpoints
resume_chunked_experiment.py.input: A three-chunk job with an example checkpoint already stored on disk.
resume_chunked_experiment.py.framing: When a long cluster array job is pre-empted mid-run, how do atomic disk checkpoints let the retry skip committed chunks and finish only the remaining work?

collect_fold_results.py.title: Merge fold results & block duplicates
collect_fold_results.py.role: Key by (config, fold, seed) with dupe guard
collect_fold_results.py.input: Example result files with identifiers and metric records.
collect_fold_results.py.framing: When collecting hundreds of result CSVs from a cluster, how do we prevent a re-submitted job from being counted twice in the fold average?

find_incomplete_runs.py.title: Flag crashed or unlaunched cluster jobs
find_incomplete_runs.py.role: Separate missing metrics vs missing runs
find_incomplete_runs.py.input: A planned list of jobs, their start records and any saved final results.
find_incomplete_runs.py.framing: Before building a thesis table, how do we tell which scheduled runs never launched and which runs started but crashed before writing final metrics?

build_grading_table.py.title: Aggregate scale MAE on matched cases
build_grading_table.py.input: A matched example sample with predictions from two image scales.
build_grading_table.py.framing: How do we verify that core, patch and cell predictions cover the exact same held-out specimens before computing the summary MAE table?

render_grading_figure.py.title: Render scale MAE summary to SVG
render_grading_figure.py.input: Three image-scale labels with example error estimates and intervals.
render_grading_figure.py.framing: How do we turn the verified scale MAE table directly into a clean, publication-ready SVG chart without manual plotting steps?

run_grading_example.py.title: Trace Case S02 from ratings to chart
run_grading_example.py.input: Two assessor grades for case S02, its fold assignment and feature vectors at three image scales.
run_grading_example.py.framing: Can a reader pick one bar in the final chart and trace Case S02 step by step from two assessor ratings (2 and 3) through Fold 1 to its 3-scale predictions?
run_grading_example.py.method: Average the two assessor grades (2.500), fit each scale's model on the other folds, predict S02 held out in Fold 1, and rebuild the 3-scale SVG chart.

bin_patch_distribution.py.title: Bin per-core patch counts [lower, upper)
bin_patch_distribution.py.input: Saved patch counts for seven example cores.
bin_patch_distribution.py.framing: How do we bin per-core patch counts into unambiguous half-open intervals [lower, upper) so boundary values (like 50) are never double-counted?

grading_figure.svg.title: Inspect the rendered 3-scale SVG chart
grading_figure.svg.input: Thirty-six held-out example predictions, twelve for each image scale.
grading_figure.svg.framing: What does the generated SVG figure look like when all 36 held-out predictions (12 synthetic cases × 3 scales) are aggregated?

verify_report_assets.py.title: Verify report files with SHA-256 hashes
verify_report_assets.py.input: Two expected report assets and a generated report directory.
verify_report_assets.py.framing: Before submitting a report or thesis, how do we verify that every referenced table and figure exists on disk and matches its expected SHA-256 fingerprint?

research_limits.md.title: Scope internal CV vs external validation
research_limits.md.input: The thesis’s internal grading and subtype comparisons and their validation design.
research_limits.md.framing: What do the internal 3-fold cross-validation results establish within this cohort, and what must be tested across independent hospitals and scanners next?

build_benchmark_bags.py.title: Build seeded PCam benchmark bags
build_benchmark_bags.py.input: Example positive and negative patches, split sizes and separate seeds.
build_benchmark_bags.py.framing: How do we assemble repeatable positive bags (1 positive patch) and negative bags (0 positive patches) with separate train/test seeds for an external benchmark?

compare_benchmark_encoders.py.title: Compare encoders on fixed PCam bags
compare_benchmark_encoders.py.input: The same labelled training and test sets, with two encoder representations.
compare_benchmark_encoders.py.framing: When we hold the seeded bag manifests and max-pooling rule fixed, how cleanly does the benchmark separate an informative encoder (1.000) from noise (0.625)?
